blocks.text: Photochemical smog (Los Angeles smog) forms in the atmosphere from NOx and volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in sunlight; it is oxidising in nature. Photochemical oxidants such as NO2, ozone and peroxyacyl nitrates (PANs) can react with and oxidise specific compounds in the atmosphere. Photochemical smog is becoming more common than classical smog (London smog) because of increasing NOx emissions. Its formation involves the reactions N2 + O2 giving 2NO; 2NO + O2 giving 2NO2; NO2 with sunlight (hv) giving NO + O; O + O2 giving O3; and alkene + O3 giving aldehyde and radicals that lead on to RC(O)OONO2, peroxyacyl nitrate.

rows: alkene + O3 gives aldehyde and radicals, leading to RC(O)OONO2 (PAN)

blocks.prompt: Write the reactions of photochemical smog formation and say why sunlight is essential (exercise Q.2e).
blocks.explanation: N2 + O2 gives 2NO; 2NO + O2 gives 2NO2; NO2 + hv gives NO + O; O + O2 gives O3; O3 with hydrocarbons gives aldehydes and radicals that end as PAN. Sunlight is needed for the photolysis of NO2, which supplies the oxygen atoms that make ozone, the main oxidant of the smog; without it the chain does not start.

items: Photochemical (Los Angeles) smog: NOx + VOCs in sunlight, oxidising (NO2, O3, PANs); now commoner than London smog. NO2 + hv gives O, O + O2 gives O3, O3 oxidises hydrocarbons towards PAN.
